title: Complexity, action, and black holes
abstract: Our earlier paper “Complexity Equals Action” conjectured that the quantum computational complexity of a holographic state is given by the classical action of a region in the bulk (the “Wheeler-DeWitt” patch). We provide calculations for the results quoted in that paper, explain how it ﬁts into a broader (tensor) network of ideas, and elaborate on the hypothesis that black holes are the fastest computers in nature. arXiv:1512.04993v2 [hep-th] 10 May 2016
